title: Conduct basic husbandry process according to industry standards

lessons.title: Daily checks on the fish farm
lessons.html:
What is husbandry?

Husbandry means looking after animals every day. On a fish farm it means checking the water, feeding, cleaning and watching the fish. Fish cannot tell us they are sick. We must look and learn the signs.

Your morning round

  1. Walk past every pond or tank at the same time each morning.
  2. Look at the fish. Are they swimming normally? Are any gasping at the top?
  3. Look for dead fish. Remove them with a net and put them in the bin for dead fish.
  4. Check that water is flowing in and out where it should.
  5. Check that aerators and paddlewheels are running.
  6. Check that screens and nets are in place and not blocked.
  7. Write what you saw on the record sheet.

Water checks

Your supervisor will show you how to use simple tools. You may read a thermometer for temperature. You may use an oxygen meter or test kit. Write every reading down with the time. If a reading is outside the range on the sheet, tell your supervisor straight away.

Gasping fish is an emergency

If many fish are at the surface gasping in the early morning, the water is low in oxygen. Switch on extra aerators if you are allowed. Stop feeding. Call your supervisor right away. Fish can die within hours.

Count the dead fish

Each day, count and write down the number of dead fish (mortalities) per tank. A sudden rise is a warning of disease or bad water. Never throw dead fish back into the water or leave them on the bank. Birds and dogs spread disease. Put them in the closed bin or the pit your farm uses.

lessons.title: Cleaning, hygiene and safe work
lessons.html:
Keep the farm clean

Dirty tanks and equipment spread disease. Clean work is part of good husbandry.

Cleaning tasks

  • Clean screens and outlet pipes so water can flow. Blocked screens can make tanks overflow and let fish escape.
  • Siphon or flush waste from the bottom of tanks as shown.
  • Remove weeds and rubbish from pond edges.
  • Scrub tank walls when your supervisor asks.

Hygiene rules

  • Each tank or pond area has its own nets and buckets. Do not mix them.
  • Dip nets and boots in the disinfectant bath when you move between units.
  • Wash your hands after touching dead fish and before eating.
  • Do not let visitors walk into the tank area without permission.

Working with chemicals

Some farms use salt, lime or disinfectants. Only use these when your supervisor tells you. Read the label or ask. Wear gloves and eye protection. Never mix chemicals. Never pour chemicals into a pond unless told to.

Safe work near water

  • Wear boots with grip. Wet concrete and pond banks are slippery.
  • Do not touch electrical pumps or plugs with wet hands. Report damaged cables.
  • Lift feed bags with bent knees and a straight back.
  • Never work alone at deep ponds.

Records

Write clearly on the daily sheet: date, tank number, feed given, dead fish, water readings and anything unusual. Good records help the manager see problems early. If you do not write it down, it did not happen.

Industry standards

Industry standards mean doing the work the same correct way every time. Follow the farm's written procedures. If you are unsure, ask before you act.

Key points

  • Check every tank at the same time every day.
  • Gasping fish means low oxygen: act and call your supervisor.
  • Remove and record dead fish daily.
  • Keep nets separate and disinfect between units.
  • Write everything on the record sheet.
